findings.title: Platform TCB identity binds to exact CI-runner kernels; accepted profile mechanism cannot admit ordinary user machines
sources: docs/coop/completion/security-fixtures.v8/profile.P-MACOS-ARM64-25G83-APFS.json /acquisition/launch/0 (refusesOn: value differs from the profile) and /signedEntries/0 (kernUuid, osversion)
findings.trigger: Any macOS host on a build other than the runner-measured build; any Linux host booting a generic-flavor Ubuntu kernel; any Linux account whose home is not ext4.
findings.consequence: NT-TCB-BOOT / NT-TCB-IDENTITY refusal at launch; the qualified support set collapses to hosts identical to GitHub-hosted runner images.
findings.counterevidence: Scope chapter defers exact baselines to DR-119/126; v2 §8.6 discloses the Linux refusal in general terms; profiles are labeled release-measured. Rejected because the accepted mechanism itself forecloses a supportable population and §8.7 forbids qualifying profiles for builds the four classes do not run.
findings.required_correction: Replace exact kernel identity with a bounded baseline plus attestation predicates (macOS major/minor range with sealed-boot and SIP checks; Linux publisher-signed kernel within a supported line, any flavor), qualify each baseline on a class that can run it, publish the actual support set at DR-119/126 and in file 10, and record csr_check SPI dependence as a release-measured risk.
findings.owner: DR-126 (Security + platform), DR-119 (Product + language + release), DR-G22

findings.title: Ancestor walk for opensip.json has no ownership or boundary check; cross-user configuration and snapshot-root injection on shared directories
sources: docs/coop/completion/host-foundation-completion.v2.md §2 lines 113-117 (walk to nearest ancestor, stop at filesystem root)
docs/coop/completion/host-foundation-completion.v2.md §1 lines 45-49 (ancestor ownership checks apply to the operational root only)
docs/coop/completion/host-foundation-completion.v2.md §3 lines 166-167 and 179-186 (layer-3 fields: pins, holds, allowedScopes, budget)
findings.trigger: User runs analyze without --project in a descendant of a shared or sticky directory (e.g. /tmp, shared CI workspace) where another principal placed opensip.json.
findings.consequence: Another principal selects component pins/holds and budget for the victim's run and makes their directory the sealed snapshot root; results can be made indeterminate or pinned to a defective component version; other users' readable files enter the report.
findings.counterevidence: Configuration is data only and cannot grant permissions; same-user ancestors are within the trust boundary. Neither answers the cross-user case.
findings.required_correction: Stop the walk at the first ancestor not owned by the invoking account or root, or at HOME/mount boundaries; require the selected project root to be owned by the invoking account; record the deciding ancestor in provenance; add G12/G18 fixtures.

findings.title: Unbounded monotonic evalHighWater advance from the wall clock; one future clock excursion permanently expires trust with no reviewed recovery
sources: docs/coop/completion/security-completion.v2.md §4.2 lines 277-288 (wall clock more than 24h ahead accepted as time passing)
findings.trigger: Dead RTC, bad NTP step or manual clock error places the wall clock in the future during any state-using operation.
findings.consequence: Every catalog, revocation list and root is expired relative to the persisted instant; no later signed payload cures it because document expiry is bounded by issue time; restore retains the floor; only out-of-band deletion of the per-user root recovers.
findings.counterevidence: Monotonic evaluation is deliberate anti-rollback; doctor reports CLOCK-REGRESSION. Neither provides recovery.
findings.required_correction: Bound the wall-clock advance (e.g. not beyond newest accepted document expiry plus tolerance, or plausibility relative to lastAccepted), or define an audited operator floor reset requiring a freshly signed payload; retain a G08 case for excursion-then-correction.

findings.title: Revocation during a live operation has journal vocabulary but no defined path to the running host; contradicts OD-112-3 alreadyRunning=refuse and chapter 03 revocation law
sources: docs/coop/completion/security-completion.v8.md §5.4 lines 250-260 and §7.5 lines 488-497 (REV only on process death)
findings.trigger: Trust refresh or imported payload revokes a component or key while an operation holding that project's lease is mid-effect.
findings.consequence: The broker keeps honoring grants to a revoked component until the operation ends; no REV trust-revoked writer exists; G09 revocation cases have no contract to execute.
findings.counterevidence: Preview worker has zero handles; new operations re-verify (revocation-refresh-allows-new-lease). Neither covers the full-product long-running case.
findings.required_correction: Specify the live path (re-read revocation counter at every effectRequest and on a bounded interval; append REV trust-revoked; cancel; teardown) or explicitly retract alreadyRunning=refuse and record the window; add G09 cases.

findings.title: Root chaining through an expired root is unspecified; dormant and air-gapped installs have no defined recovery after 365 days
findings.trigger: Install presents a payload carrying root N+1 after root N has expired at tEval.
findings.consequence: Either permanent refusal requiring fresh core install, or an unwritten rule that could weaken anti-rollback; DR-G08's claim that trust survives expiry has no clause to test.
findings.counterevidence: G15 final join covers root admission negatives and origin/previous-version consistency, not expiry chaining.
findings.required_correction: Add an explicit rule (intermediate root expiry ignored during chaining; newest root must be unexpired at tEval; rootVersion anti-rollback holds) with one retained case.

findings.title: D-371 Rust depth is jointly unsatisfiable with no-repository-execution and no-confinement under the accepted permission model
sources: docs/v2/architecture/10-mvp-and-future-scope.md table rows Native language depth and Exclusions lines 39, 45; lines 74-77
docs/coop/artifacts/permission-truth-tables.v7.json lines 143-149 and 181-195 (PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED bounded to admitted tree; PT-NET-EGRESS)
docs/coop/completion/security-completion.v1.md §6.1 lines 556-563 (six tokens DISCLOSURE-ONLY) and §6.3 lines 578-580 (PR-6 empty trigger set)
findings.trigger: Authoring the Rust capability cells at DR-118 that require cfg/proc-macro expansion.
findings.consequence: Either Rust semantics are far shallower than promised, or a grant runs third-party repository code with the user's ambient authority under a token vocabulary that cannot enforce the promised network-disabled bound.
findings.counterevidence: Rows DR-117/118/119 are OPEN for full product and freeze law 11 governs; the tension is known in pieces but never recorded as a contradiction.
findings.required_correction: Record a product decision before capability authoring: accept a declared Rust depth without repository execution, or admit a confinement primitive with enforcement evidence (which reopens DR-128 scope), and add a principal class for repository-controlled code to the threat model.
findings.owner: DR-117/DR-118/DR-119 (Product + language + security), with DR-105 and DR-128

findings.title: Stage-1 closed vocabularies refuse stage-2 extensions and the compatibility matrix promises no bridge; contradicts D-371's no-incompatible-state-models statement
sources: docs/coop/completion/security_unit_lib_v8.py admit_root lines 250-258 (TR-REPAIR typed absence and kernelAttestationKeys=[] are refusals)
docs/coop/artifacts/permission-truth-tables.v7.json lines 143 and 153 (fs.write.project RESERVED; closed at seven)
docs/coop/completion/compatibility-matrix.completed.v5.json /rows S-SCHEMA, S-CTRL, S-STATE (readers [1,1], no cross-major bridge)
findings.trigger: Publishing a root with an active TR-REPAIR role, a third effect class, a project-write token or a new journal record type for repair/import.
findings.consequence: Stage-1 hosts refuse the documents; the first stage-2 capable host is a fresh install, not an update.
findings.counterevidence: DR-110/111 are OPEN for full product and the reference architecture discloses no upgrade continuity for the preview.
findings.required_correction: Record a stage-transition contract at DR-107/110/111 that reserves extension points now (e.g. active TR-REPAIR admissible under stated key policy; effect-class registry; token extension rule) and defines migration or honest discard of stage-1 state.

findings.title: Adopted manifest and evidence annotations self-describe as not adopted or carry stale digests; duplicate section numbers in security v8
sources: docs/coop/completion/security-completion.v8.md headings at lines 713-723 and 731-814 (two sections numbered 10, 11, 12)
findings.trigger: A reader or later checker relies on the self-description or the observed digest.
findings.consequence: Misreading of adoption state; a future heading-selector pin on §10-§12 fails the unique-heading rule.
findings.counterevidence: Whole-review v6 explicitly disposes stale standing strings as residue and records the 54f3 digest.
findings.required_correction: Pin-only successor that corrects the status strings, removes or explains observedSha256, renumbers the appended sections, and refreshes the freeze v6 pre-review block.
findings.confidence: high for the text; digests not recomputed by me

findings.title: Decided offline refresh cliff and doctor exit-zero-on-defect are not disclosed at the product-facing surfaces
findings.trigger: Air-gapped install exceeds the revocation freshness floor; CI gates doctor on its exit code.
findings.consequence: Already-verified analysis stops without a payload import; CI passes with environment defects unless it parses report.outcome.
findings.counterevidence: Both are decided under OD-112-2 and the frozen D9 vocabulary.
findings.required_correction: State the refresh obligation in the scope chapter's local-first row and in doctor output; add CI guidance that gates on report.outcome.

strengths: Fence-then-lease non-blocking handoff and GC census (security v8 §5.4; lifecycle-carrier.contract.v2.json callbacks) eliminate the fence-wait deadlock class and are exercised on real SQLite.
Witness reconciliation as an exception-free boundary with a closed shape and complete action table (security_unit_lib_v8.py 273-343).
HE-1 ordered algorithm: durable RA and intent before effect, footprint-decided recovery, closed outcome vocabulary, receipt tied to record position (v8 §7.5; he1_recover).
Effective policy digests both raw sources, deny-by-absence, whole-segment narrowing, refusal yields zero grants (v8 §6.11; merge_policy).
Single root admission boundary with use-side recheck; a raw dictionary can never verify (admit_root_document, recheck_admitted_root).
Honest confinement labeling: disclosure-only cells, worker declared TCB not sandbox, brokered route declared voluntary; this honesty exposes SEC-06 rather than hiding it.
TypeScript worker launch posture: sealed VFS only, no repository execution, environment from empty, no addons, no global search paths, one-shot process (delivery.v2 §authority; broker-bootstrap v2).
Separate monotonic trust database never restored by generation rollback; detected and undetected rollback cases stated (v8 §5.5).
Archive profile closed to file/dir/symlink with hard-link and PAX forms forbidden; stage and result files admitted on nlink==1, owner and size via held directory fds.
